llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: L-Ascorbic acid is a solid analyte and is dispensed directly by Quantos into the KCl electrolyte vial. The solution is prepared immediately before analysis because aqueous vitamin C is sensitive to air, light, elevated temperature, and metal contamination. Nitrogen purge reduces oxygen-mediated degradation and oxygen-reduction background current.
assumptions: Vitamin C is assumed to be L-ascorbic acid, molecular weight 176.12 g/mol, rather than a vitamin-C salt or formulation containing excipients.
KCl is assumed to be available as a dry Quantos-compatible solid, and L-ascorbic acid is assumed to be loadable as a dry Quantos-compatible solid in separate cartridges.
Water is assumed to be available as a pump-compatible liquid on syringe-pump channel 1.
The actual recipe KCl mass required for 0.100 M in 15.000 mL is 111.8265 mg. The KCl recipe and checklist mass should be corrected from 167.745 mg to 111.8265 mg before execution.
Nitrogen is assumed to be available to the substation purge function.
The pH is expected to be acidic due to dissolved ascorbic acid; no buffer is used because no compatible buffer components are specified as available solid reagents.
The platinum working electrode is available as requested, despite the generic schema example listing a gold working electrode.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: The initially calculated 0.100 M KCl mass would be 0.100 mol/L × 0.015 L × 74.551 g/mol = 0.1118265 g = 111.8265 mg. However, the planned mass must match the recipe concentration. Corrected planned KCl mass for 0.100 M is 111.8265 mg; the recipe mass should be interpreted as 111.8265 mg, not 167.745 mg.

Required moles = 0.00500 mol/L × 0.0150 L = 0.0000750 mol. Required mass = 0.0000750 mol × 176.12 g/mol = 0.013209 g = 13.209 mg. Dispensing 13.209 mg into a final 15.000 mL volume gives 0.00500 M L-ascorbic acid.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: One experiment vial and one electrochemical slot are used. Two solids are dispensed through Quantos, which is within the maximum of eight solid cartridges. Each solid mass is below the 200 mg per-cartridge maximum: KCl is 167.745 mg and L-ascorbic acid is 13.209 mg. One pump-compatible liquid, water, is dispensed through one of four available liquid channels. Water volume is exactly 15.000 mL, satisfying the required vial fill volume for electrode contact. The selected aqueous reference electrode is Ag/AgCl in 3 M KCl. The requested platinum 2 mm working electrode and platinum wire counter electrode are specified. The plan uses one of the three available parallel electrochemical slots.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No drying step is required because no material is deposited on the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: No electrode deposition is performed because vitamin C is measured as a dissolved analyte in the prepared electrolyte.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Load KCl into Quantos cartridge position 1 and dispense the calculated mass into a clean 20 mL experiment vial. Load L-ascorbic acid into Quantos cartridge position 2 and dispense it into the same vial. Dispense 15.000 mL water through liquid channel 1. Mix by ultrasound for 120 seconds until all visible solids are dissolved. Immediately transfer the vial to the electrochemical substation, measure and record the pre-test pH, nitrogen-purge the solution for 300 seconds to reduce dissolved oxygen, and then conduct the CV. Measure and record pH again after the fifth cycle.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.100 M KCl aqueous supporting electrolyte provides ionic conductivity while requiring only a single supported solid salt and water. A 5.00 mM L-ascorbic acid concentration provides a measurable oxidation response at a 2 mm platinum electrode while minimizing analyte mass and electrode fouling. The potential window from -0.100 V to +0.700 V versus Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) is selected to include the expected irreversible ascorbic-acid oxidation wave on platinum while avoiding unnecessarily positive potentials where substantial water oxidation and platinum-surface changes may occur. A 50 mV/s scan rate and 5 mV potential increment provide adequate definition of the oxidation wave. Five cycles are explicitly specified as requested; progressive loss of the anodic signal is possible because ascorbic acid oxidation is not fully reversible and its oxidation products may foul platinum. AUTO current range is selected because the exact oxidation current depends on electrode condition, analyte aging, dissolved oxygen, and mass transport.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The requested configuration is analyte_in_electrolyte because vitamin C is to be dissolved directly in a supporting electrolyte and measured in the experiment vial rather than deposited on an electrode.

metadata.description: Five-cycle aqueous cyclic voltammetry measurement of L-ascorbic acid dissolved in 0.100 M potassium chloride supporting electrolyte using a 2 mm platinum working electrode, platinum wire counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl (3 M KCl) reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Cyclic Voltammetry of Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid) in 0.100 M KCl
metadata.user_prompt: Perform a cyclic voltammetry experiment to characterize vitamin C as an analyte dissolved in the electrolyte. The vitamin C should be prepared in the electrolyte and measured using the electrochemical substation. Use the available platinum working electrode (d = 2 mm), platinum counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl in KCL 3M reference electrode. Select appropriate electrolyte composition, vitamin C concentration, CV parameters, mixing/preparation steps, and safety precautions based on the capabilities and constraints provided in the system context. The resulting experiment must be directly executable by the CVLab platform. Also, please perform 5 cycles.

cross_contamination_risks: Ascorbic acid oxidation products can adsorb on platinum and alter subsequent voltammograms; polish, wash, and dry the platinum working electrode after the experiment.
KCl residue on electrodes or in the vial can contaminate later low-ionic-strength measurements; rinse thoroughly with water.
Avoid transferring material between Quantos cartridges; dedicate the cartridge positions to KCl and L-ascorbic acid for this run.
handling_precautions: Wear laboratory coat, safety glasses, and suitable gloves while loading Quantos cartridges and handling electrolyte.
Avoid generating dust when loading KCl and ascorbic acid cartridges; clean spilled powders promptly.
Prepare vitamin C solution immediately before measurement and minimize exposure to air and light because ascorbic acid oxidizes over time.
Confirm electrode immersion in the full 15 mL aqueous solution before initiating the CV.
Polish, wash, and dry the platinum working electrode before the measurement to reduce carryover and fouling.
Use nitrogen purge only with appropriate laboratory ventilation and verify that the gas outlet is safely directed.
hazards: Potassium chloride and L-ascorbic acid are low-hazard solids but may cause eye or respiratory irritation as dusts.
The platinum electrodes and glassware may be damaged by mishandling.
Electrical and moving robotic components of the electrochemical substation present pinch and equipment hazards.
Nitrogen purging can displace oxygen in poorly ventilated spaces.
waste_disposal: Collect the post-CV aqueous KCl/ascorbic acid solution in the designated aqueous non-heavy-metal electrochemical waste container unless local procedures require a different waste stream.
Do not return used solution to reagent reservoirs.
Rinse electrodes and vial with water after the experiment; collect the first rinse as aqueous electrochemical waste if required by local laboratory procedure.
